blocks.text: Quick verdict

Decodo is the better choice for scraping, SERP and e-commerce data: its pool is nearly four times larger, it is cheaper at 10 GB ($35 against $45 PAYG), and its scraping APIs handle harder targets. NodeMaven is the better choice for social media management, multi-accounting and anti-detect browser work, where pre-screened IPs and long sticky sessions reduce bans, and its $2.20/GB monthly rate undercuts Decodo's $2.75 at 100 GB. NodeMaven also rolls over unused traffic, which Decodo's plans do not.

NodeMaven and Decodo both serve self-service buyers, but they optimise for different things. Decodo optimises for breadth: a 115M+ residential pool, ZIP and ASN targeting, datacenter, ISP and mobile networks, and scraping APIs. NodeMaven optimises for IP quality: a 30M+ residential and 250K mobile pool where every IP is screened before you get it, with long sticky sessions, rollover and cashback. This comparison shows which approach suits scraping and which suits account work.

blocks.text: NodeMaven in 2026: what you get

NodeMaven competes on IP quality rather than pool size. Every residential and mobile IP passes through its IP Quality Filter before it is assigned, with three strictness levels, and the company reports a 95% clean-IP rate. Proxyway's testing found the filter lowered fraud scores noticeably on sticky sessions. The pool is 30M+ residential plus 250K mobile IPs in 150+ countries, traffic rolls over, and you get up to 10% cashback on used gigabytes plus a guarantee that pays out for bad proxies.

Strengths: IP Quality Filter screens IPs before you get them; Long sticky sessions for account work; Traffic rollover and cashback; Quality guarantee that pays for bad IPs. Weak spots: Smaller pool than mass-market networks; No datacenter proxies; Pay-as-you-go rate is double the plan rate.
Decodo in 2026: what you get

Decodo is the 2024 rebrand of Smartproxy, one of the most popular mid-market providers. Its residential network is advertised at 115 million IPs across 195+ locations, and independent benchmarks put its success rate around 99.9% with sub-second response times. Every plan includes the full pool plus city, state, ZIP and ASN targeting, and the dashboard is one of the easiest to set up. Decodo also sells datacenter, ISP and mobile proxies and a family of scraping APIs.

Strengths: Large 115M+ pool at a mid-market price; Near-perfect success rates in independent tests; Clean, fast self-service onboarding; Scraping APIs available when raw proxies are not enough. Weak spots: Plan traffic does not roll over; Published pricing stops at 100 GB; beyond that you need a quote; More expensive per GB than budget brands.
Pricing: NodeMaven vs Decodo

NodeMaven charges $4.50/GB pay-as-you-go and $2.20/GB on monthly plans, with residential and mobile traffic on one balance. A $3.50 trial includes 750 MB. Unused traffic rolls over, and you earn up to 10% cashback on used traffic. ISP proxies start at $2.99 per IP with unlimited traffic.

Decodo sells residential traffic at $4/GB pay-as-you-go with no commitment, or on monthly plans: 3 GB for $11.25 ($3.75/GB), 10 GB for $35, 25 GB at $3.25/GB, 50 GB for $150 and 100 GB for $275 ($2.75/GB). Top-ups are billed at your plan's rate, so you are not pushed into the next tier.

For a 10 GB month, Decodo costs about $35 while NodeMaven costs about $45, so Decodo saves around 22%. For a 100 GB month, NodeMaven costs about $220 while Decodo costs about $275, so NodeMaven saves around 20%. The sticker price is only half of it. NodeMaven's unused traffic carries forward, while Decodo's does not (plan traffic resets monthly; payg for bursty work), so if your usage swings from month to month NodeMaven can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Decodo has the bigger advertised network, 115M+ residential IPs against 30M+ residential + 250K mobile for NodeMaven, roughly 3.8 times larger. Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, NodeMaven lists 150+ countries and Decodo lists 195+. On targeting, NodeMaven offers country, region, city and ISP, while Decodo offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, NodeMaven offers rotating or long sticky sessions (multi-day), and Decodo offers rotating or sticky sessions with configurable duration. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Decodo wins. The deciding factor for Decodo: a large pool and near-perfect benchmark success rates. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: the quality filter matters less for high-rotation crawling.

SERP and rank tracking: Decodo wins. The deciding factor for Decodo: a dedicated SERP scraping API plus city targeting. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: workable, but you pay a premium for filtering you may not need.

Social media and multi-account management: NodeMaven wins. The deciding factor for NodeMaven: pre-screened, low-fraud-score IPs with long sticky sessions. The limitation on the Decodo side: sticky sessions, sub-users and an easy dashboard.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: ZIP targeting and a ready-made e-commerce API. How NodeMaven compares: fine for light checks.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Decodo wins. The deciding factor for Decodo: wide coverage with city and ASN targeting. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: good quality but a smaller pool.
Tight budgets: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With NodeMaven: mid-priced on plans, expensive on PAYG. With Decodo: it is mid-priced, not cheap. Run the same small test on both before committing.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB. Decodo: Free trial (about 100 MB) on residential. Verification and payment rules differ too. NodeMaven: Standard. Decodo: Light KYC; checks on some targets. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test NodeMaven and Decodo before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle NodeMaven vs Decodo faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB; Decodo: free trial (about 100 MB) on residential).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, NodeMaven comes out ahead in 1, Decodo in 4, and 1 is a tie. That makes Decodo the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: NodeMaven is strongest for social media and multi-account management, while Decodo is strongest for small and mid-size scraping teams. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
